title: DPSW-Sketch: A Differentially Private Sketch Framework for Frequency Estimation over Sliding Windows

problem.claim: Privately estimate arbitrary-item frequencies and identify heavy hitters over a sliding window while using small space and providing a provable privacy guarantee.

contributions.claim: DPSW-Sketch is a differentially private sliding-window framework based on the count-min sketch.
The framework supports frequency and heavy-hitter queries with bounded errors in sublinear time and space with respect to the window size.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on five real-world and synthetic datasets report significantly better utility-privacy trade-offs than state-of-the-art methods.

narrative_sequence.summary: Sliding windows retain only the most recent w stream items for analysis.
Algorithms must track statistics accurately with small space, and sensitive streams require provable privacy.
The paper targets private frequency estimation and heavy-hitter identification over sliding windows.
DPSW-Sketch uses a differentially private count-min-sketch-based framework with bounded-error, sublinear-time and sublinear-space query approximation.
Experiments report improved utility-privacy trade-offs against state-of-the-art methods.

source_observation.claim: The proposed framework jointly addresses privacy, bounded query error, and sublinear resource use for sliding-window streams.

interpretation.claim: Streaming analytics methods may need to treat privacy and resource constraints as coupled design requirements.

application.claim: For sensitive streaming systems, consider sketch-based methods that explicitly expose privacy and window-size resource trade-offs.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish performance outside the stated frequency and heavy-hitter queries or outside sliding-window streams.
